newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH C.BANK SAYS NO NEAR-TERM ZLOTY RISE -PAPER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH C.BANK SAYS NO NEAR-TERM ZLOTY RISE -PAPER.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland will not allow the zloty to firm in the near term -- neither on the market nor through slower monthly devaluation, the bank's deputy head said.
"A firming of the zloty is unacceptable," Rzeczpospolita daily quoted on Tuesday Witold Kozinski as saying.

A stronger zloty would boost the already fast growing Polish imports and widen the trade gap, which could reach five percent of Poland's gross domestic product this year against one percent in 1996, Kozinski was reported as saying.
"Such (five percent of GDP) trade gap would not be a drama, but if its growth rate continued, the situation could become dangerous," Kozinski was quoted as saying.
The finance ministry estimates the trade gap might reach 3-3.5 percentof GDP in 1997.
Kozinski said that to restore balance between imports and exports growth the bank was cooling down domestic demand by keeping high real interest rates with no near-term prospects of their reduction.

Kozinski was reported as saying that the bank did not want to raise interest rates further because such a move would undermine economic growth as well as trigger an inflow of short-term foreign capital.
Kozinski said that instead the central bank raised obligatory reserve levels for banks, and that he expected the move to reduce money supply by several billion zlotys.
"We hope that the rising of the reserves will result in smaller domestic demand and a slower growth of the trade gap," Kozinski was quoted as saying.
